clue.text: Look on president with certain urge to fit in

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
certain means sure

explanation.surface: Someone watches a president whose confident drive is simply to belong.
explanation.definitionFit: Peer pressure is the social push to conform with the group around you, an urge to belong.

clue.text: Suffering love in goin' away

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for love sits inside the clipped word for going away

parts.note: going away is passing; with the dropped g of goin' it becomes passin'
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A lover pines while their partner heads off, dialect and all.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in goin' is the hint that the synonym also drops its final G.
explanation.definitionFit: The Passion is the suffering of Christ before the crucifixion, and passion once meant suffering generally.

clue.text: Target wild mice confined to a particular area

parts.note: an end is an aim or target

indicators.note: wild means the letters of mice run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone aims at untamed mice that live only in one region.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic species or disease is native to, and restricted to, one locality.

clue.text: Like a bat out of hell spread around unfettered tosh

definitions.text: Like a bat out of hell

indicators.note: around says the spread goes round the outside of the jumbled letters

parts.note: paste is a spread, as in fish paste on toast

indicators.note: unfettered means freed from restraint, so the letters of tosh are let loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone frantically spreads nonsense that has broken free of all restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a verb about scattering the tosh; here it is the noun, a paste you put on bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a bat out of hell is an idiom for extremely fast, which is what posthaste means.

clue.text: Cut up manuscript for short trials

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for cut is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it

explanation.surface: An editor chops up a manuscript to make brief trial copies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' looks like one verb meaning chop; it splits into AXE and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Exams is the clipped form of examinations, which are tests or trials of knowledge, hence short.

clue.text: Rinse so rejuvenated us?

indicators.note: rejuvenated means made over anew, so the letters of rinse so are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An older person wonders if a hair rinse will make them look young again.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'us?' is the voice of older people themselves, the question mark flagging the playful self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Seniors are elderly people, the 'us' who might be using a rinse to look younger.

clue.text: Dish to stir vigorously with what's central to stock

indicators.note: vigorously suggests violent stirring, so the letters of to stir are shaken into a new order
what's central to points at the middle letter of the word stock

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: beat the dish hard with the heart of the stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock with constant stirring.

clue.text: Imagine ship's beak in iron mount

parts.note: to picture something is to imagine it

indicators.note: in places the ship's beak inside the symbol for iron

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a ram is the beak on the prow of a warship used to strike others

explanation.surface: Picture a ship's prow set in an iron mounting.
explanation.definitionFit: A mount is the border or frame that holds and displays a picture.

clue.text: Team on bat is showing guts

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the team word follows the word for batting

parts.note: a side that is batting in cricket is said to be in
a side is a team
is shortened to 's gives S

explanation.surface: A team on the batting side shows real courage.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is said to be 'in'. 'Guts' tempts as courage but means the innards.
explanation.definitionFit: Insides are the internal organs, the innards or guts of a body.

clue.text: One initially confused after name's lost

definitions.text: One initially confused after name's lost

indicators.note: after puts the remaining letters behind the rearranged ones
lost means astray, so the letters of name's wander into a new order

parts.note: name's read as names, without the apostrophe
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of confused

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled at first after forgetting a name.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesic person suffers memory loss, so would be bewildered once they forget who they are.

clue.text: Talk change taking on board core elements of oath

indicators.note: taking on board means accepting something inside, so the core letters go into the word for change

parts.note: a conversion is a change from one form to another

indicators.note: core elements of picks out the middle letters of oath

explanation.surface: A discussion shifts once the heart of a vow is accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversation is an informal exchange of views between people, a chat.

clue.text: I'll feature in trusty husband's fantastic achievement

indicators.note: feature in means appear within, so the I goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a trump is a dependable person, a trusty good sort
I'll read as I will: the letter I is what will feature
H is the abbreviation for husband, as in marriage registers

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of their part in a reliable husband's splendid feat.
explanation.walkthrough: A trump, in old-fashioned British slang, is a reliable, generous person.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great success or victory, an outstanding accomplishment.

clue.text: Take up crop

definitions.meaning: first sense: to take up a hem or garment, making it shorter
second sense: to crop is to cut short

explanation.walkthrough: Both phrases sound agricultural or hobbyist, but each is just a way of cutting something down in length.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten is to reduce in length, whether by raising a hem or by trimming.

clue.text: Run academic institute with college of ancient writing

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for institute

explanation.surface: Someone manages a scholarly institute plus a college devoted to old scripts.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes are the letters of old Germanic alphabets, so runic describes that early script.

clue.text: Soft rock giving melodramatic serial's tenor

parts.note: a soap is a melodramatic TV serial; with 's it gives SOAPS
tenor in the sense of general drift or character means tone

explanation.surface: A mellow rock song lends a TV soap its mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft rock' suggests easy-listening music, and tenor a singer; both are misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapstone, or steatite, is a soft talc-rich stone that feels soapy and carves easily.

clue.text: A new slant regarding hors d'oeuvre, forse

parts.note: to tip is to tilt or slant
as to means regarding or concerning

explanation.surface: A fresh angle on starters, perhaps, slipped into Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: Forse is Italian for perhaps, so it marks an Italian example of an hors d'oeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter course of cured meats, olives and the like served before the main meal.

clue.text: Behind romp with woman in Paris, wanton at heart

parts.note: a romp is a bit of fun
dame is French for lady or woman

indicators.note: at heart takes the middle letters of wanton

explanation.surface: A saucy frolic with a Parisian lady, lustful deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a preposition but is the noun for one's bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundament is a formal or jocular word for the buttocks or anus, a person's behind.

clue.text: Letter from Kyriakos Mitsotakis on pure source of energy?

parts.note: Kyriakos Mitsotakis is the Greek prime minister, so his letter is a Greek one, nu
clear means pure, as in clear water

explanation.surface: A Greek prime minister's letter about clean energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter from' suggests correspondence; it means a letter of his alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear power, from fission in reactors, is one source of electrical energy, hence the question mark for a describing word.

clue.text: A lake I love when changing components of breathing apparatus?

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: when changing means the letters of love are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone's feelings shift for a lake as their breathing gear changes.
explanation.walkthrough: The breathing apparatus is the lungs, not scuba gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Alveoli are the tiny air sacs in the lungs where gas exchange takes place.

clue.text: Drivers with freight good to go

indicators.note: to go means the letter for good is to leave the word for freight

parts.note: goods are freight, as in a goods train

explanation.surface: Lorry drivers carrying cargo ready for departure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drivers' suggests lorry drivers with freight; it means golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, woods are long-hitting clubs, the driver being the number one wood.

clue.text: Justify fighting tub-thumping?

parts.note: war is fighting
tub-thumping is ranting, loud impassioned speechmaking

explanation.surface: Can belligerent speechmaking ever be defended?
explanation.definitionFit: To warrant something is to give grounds for it, to make it reasonable.

clue.text: Theoretically propane combusts

indicators.note: combusts means burns up, so the letters of propane blow apart and re-form

explanation.surface: In principle, propane bursts into flame.
explanation.definitionFit: On paper means in theory, as planned rather than as it turns out in practice.

clue.text: Company very into beers finding niches

indicators.note: into places the company and very letters inside the beers

parts.note: ales are beers

explanation.surface: A brewing firm finds its market gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcoves are recesses set into a wall, small nooks or niches.

clue.text: Ditches such as you often see in gardens

definitions.meaning: first sense: to shed is to cast off or get rid of

definitions.text: such as you often see in gardens
definitions.meaning: second sense: garden huts for tools and pots

explanation.walkthrough: Ditches suggests trenches, which you might also see in gardens; the verb sense is to discard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for casting off and a noun for small wooden outbuildings used for storage.

clue.text: Soldier to sulk protecting wall

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
a pet is a fit of sulking, as in in a pet

explanation.surface: A soldier is about to sulk behind a defensive wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low barrier along a roof, bridge or rampart that shields or guards people.

clue.text: Some disgrace, yes, or else a carbuncle

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A new building is called a scandal, yes, or else a monstrosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carbuncle' recalls Prince Charles calling a planned extension to London's National Gallery a 'monstrous carbuncle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle, figuratively, is an ugly building, an unsightly blot on the landscape.

clue.text: Commonly bubbly is phoney and mostly rubbish

parts.note: a sham is something phoney

indicators.note: mostly means take all but the last letter

parts.note: pooh is an exclamation dismissing something as rubbish

explanation.surface: Cheap fizz is fake and largely garbage.
explanation.walkthrough: Shampoo is informal British slang for champagne; 'commonly' marks the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a jokey colloquial name for champagne, the sparkling wine.

clue.text: What snooker coach does is perhaps obsessive?

parts.note: what a coach does is train, so trains
a snooker player is a potter, one who pots balls

explanation.surface: A snooker coach's job turns out to be fanatical.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits as what a coach does to a snooker player: trains potter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainspotter is a hobbyist who logs train numbers, a byword for an obsessive enthusiast.
